summary: Checks whether a value is **not** the `NaN` number.
description: `nonNaN(value)` is the same test as `!isNaN(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not the `NaN` number; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonNaN(0); // => true
nonNaN("abc"); // => true
nonNaN(undefined); // => true
nonNaN(NaN); // => false
nonNaN(0 / 0); // => false
```
